title: Harbor and Kitchen
premise: Jude Marchetti ghostwrites celebrity memoirs, erasing herself into other people's stories — until a commission to write the memoirs of chef Theo Vance, the man whose letter she never answered eleven years ago, forces her back to the coastal town where they grew up. As she drafts his life in his voice, a lost letter surfaces from his late mother revealing that Jude's silence was engineered by someone who profited from their separation. To claim her own story, Jude must forgive the girl who chose survival over love and confess the truth before Theo's book — and their second chance — goes to print. The novel ends with Jude publishing her first book under her own name, with Theo's kitchen as its dedication page.
about_author: Marguerite Hartwell is the pen name of a former ghostwriter who spent a decade lending her voice to other people's memories before claiming her own. She writes from a rented cottage on the Maine coast, where the fog does most of the editing.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In New York, Jude accepts a lucrative contract to ghostwrite celebrity chef Theo Vance's memoir, telling herself eleven years is long enough to bury what happened between them. When she arrives at his harbor-side restaurant and hears him say her name, the past cracks open. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism — she has walked willingly into the one story she can't survive anonymously.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Jude and Theo. While sorting his mother's belongings for the memoir's early chapters, Theo finds an unopened letter addressed to Jude, postmarked the summer she disappeared from Harbor Neck. Reading it together, they realize her abrupt departure wasn't cowardice but something orchestrated. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion — memory itself becomes untrustworthy, and so do the people who shaped it.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude confronts her old mentor, literary agent Camille Roth, who admits she intercepted the letter to keep Jude hungry, dependent, and ghostwriting — survival purchased with Jude's stolen future. Shattered, Jude nearly flees again, repeating the old pattern, until she reads her own reflection in the memoir draft: she has been writing everyone's forgiveness except her own. Emotional beat: the dark night of the self, where identity and complicity collide.

chapters.title: Dedication Page
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, closing with Jude's. At the memoir's launch dinner, Theo abandons the prepared text and tells the room the true story — including the letter, the lie, and the woman who wrote every beautiful sentence of it. Jude steps out of the shadows, claims authorship aloud for the first time, and forgives the girl in the mirror. Emotional beat: release and arrival — time finally runs out in their favor, and the last line is her name on a cover that is hers.
